walkthroughs.body_html:
Celestial Observation — a core area of GCSE Astronomy.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Celestial Observation brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Celestial Observation.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: How many planets are in the Solar System (IAU 2006)?
Who proposed the heliocentric model in 1543?
options: Galileo
Copernicus
Kepler
Ptolemy

mcqs.q: What does a telescope's aperture primarily determine?
options: Comets are larger than asteroids.
Magnification.
Light-gathering ability and angular resolution.
How far it can see.

mcqs.q: What is the 'habitable zone' around a star?
options: The region where liquid water could exist on a planet's surface.
How far it can see.
Where life definitely exists.
Where humans could survive without spacesuits.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between an asteroid and a comet?
options: How far it can see.
Comets are larger than asteroids.
They are the same object with different names.
Asteroids are rocky/metallic; comets contain ice that vaporises near the Sun, producing a tail.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Astronomical Unit (AU)”?
options: Like a planet but has not cleared its orbital neighbourhood; includes Pluto, Eris, Ceres.
Sun-centred model of the Solar System established by Copernicus in 1543.
Body orbiting the Sun, massive enough to be spherical, that has cleared its orbital neighbourhood.
Average Earth-Sun distance, about 150 million km, used to measure Solar System distances.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Planet (IAU 2006)”?
options: G-type main-sequence star at the centre of the Solar System, containing 99.86% of its mass.
Like a planet but has not cleared its orbital neighbourhood; includes Pluto, Eris, Ceres.
Body orbiting the Sun, massive enough to be spherical, that has cleared its orbital neighbourhood.
Sun-centred model of the Solar System established by Copernicus in 1543.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Solar System”?
options: The Sun and everything bound to it by gravity: 8 planets, dwarf planets, moons, asteroids and comets.
Average Earth-Sun distance, about 150 million km, used to measure Solar System distances.
G-type main-sequence star at the centre of the Solar System, containing 99.86% of its mass.
Body orbiting the Sun, massive enough to be spherical, that has cleared its orbital neighbourhood.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Sun”?
options: The Sun and everything bound to it by gravity: 8 planets, dwarf planets, moons, asteroids and comets.
G-type main-sequence star at the centre of the Solar System, containing 99.86% of its mass.
Like a planet but has not cleared its orbital neighbourhood; includes Pluto, Eris, Ceres.
Body orbiting the Sun, massive enough to be spherical, that has cleared its orbital neighbourhood.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Heliocentric model”?
options: Like a planet but has not cleared its orbital neighbourhood; includes Pluto, Eris, Ceres.
Average Earth-Sun distance, about 150 million km, used to measure Solar System distances.
Sun-centred model of the Solar System established by Copernicus in 1543.
The Sun and everything bound to it by gravity: 8 planets, dwarf planets, moons, asteroids and comets.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Dwarf planet”?
options: Body orbiting the Sun, massive enough to be spherical, that has cleared its orbital neighbourhood.
Sun-centred model of the Solar System established by Copernicus in 1543.
The Sun and everything bound to it by gravity: 8 planets, dwarf planets, moons, asteroids and comets.
Like a planet but has not cleared its orbital neighbourhood; includes Pluto, Eris, Ceres.

mcqs.q: Approximately how many million kilometres is 1 AU?
options: 150 million km
75 million km
120 million km
225 million km
